:::{#thm-entropy-chain-rule}
#### Chain rule for entropy

For discrete random variables $X$ and $Y$,

$$H(X, Y) = H(X) + H(Y \mid X).$$

:::

::: {.proof}

Use the notation of @def-joint-entropy and @def-entropy-given-value.
With probability $1$, $p(X, Y) = p(X) \, p(Y \mid X)$ and $p(X, Y) > 0$,
so

$$-\log p(X, Y) = -\log p(X) - \log p(Y \mid X).$$

Both terms on the right are nonnegative,
so the expectation of the sum is the sum of the expectations:

$$
\begin{aligned}
H(X, Y)
&= \E{-\log p(X, Y)} \\
&= \E{-\log p(X)} + \E{-\log p(Y \mid X)} \\
&= H(X) + H(Y \mid X).
\end{aligned}
$$

:::
